chunks: Ali narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

While the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was sitting in the mosque, a man entered, stood, and performed salat, but he did not complete his bowing or his prostration. So he صلى الله عليه وآله said: “He pecked like the pecking of a crow. If this man dies while his salat is like this, he will surely die upon other than my religion.”

key_terms.دِينِي: my religion, meaning the religion brought by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.صَلَاتُهُ: his salat, referring to the quality and manner of his prayer
key_terms.نَقَرَ: he pecked; a metaphor for hurried, improper movement
key_terms.ٱلْغُرَابِ: the crow, used in the comparison for rapid pecking
key_terms.ٱلْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the setting in which the event occurred

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله say about rushing through ruku' and sujud in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns performing salat hastily without properly completing ruku' and sujud. It stresses that valid worship requires calmness and fulfillment of its essential acts, and it portrays neglect of these fundamentals as a grave departure from the Prophetic way.
